context.org_context: The reader is a product manager at a 40-person B2B software company running two products: Atlas CRM, an AI copilot embedded in a sales CRM, and FieldKit, a mobile inspection app for utility crews. They read both to move the two products forward and to sharpen general AI-product craft.

parked.label: On-device dictation benchmarks, parked for later

items.title: Why sales reps rewrite the AI's email: field notes from 12 CRM copilot rollouts
items.snippet: Interviews across 12 enterprise rollouts found reps send only 18 percent of AI-drafted emails without edits, and trust collapses after a single hallucinated detail about an account. The teams that recovered adoption did it with visible source citations inside the draft, not better models.

items.title: Grounding copilots in CRM records: retrieval patterns that cut fabricated fields by 40 percent
items.snippet: A practical walkthrough of scoping retrieval to the account object graph before generation: fabricated field values dropped 40 percent and p95 latency held under 900 ms after the team moved from whole-CRM embedding search to typed record lookups.

items.title: Offline-first is a product decision: how inspection apps survive 12-hour connectivity gaps
items.snippet: A case study of utility crews in northern Ontario, where 12-hour dead zones are routine: conflict resolution rules, not sync technology, drove support tickets down 35 percent. Argues PMs should spec merge behavior per field type instead of leaving it to the sync library.

items.title: On-device speech models now handle inspection dictation at 1.2x realtime on mid-tier Android
items.snippet: Benchmarks of three distilled speech models on a Pixel 7a and a Galaxy A54 show inspection-style dictation transcribing at 1.2x realtime with a 4.1 percent word error rate, no network required. Voice-to-form is now viable for field workflows without a cloud round trip.

items.title: PRD teardown: specifying a copilot feature when the baseline is a blank text box
items.snippet: Walks through a real PRD for an email-drafting copilot: how to define acceptance criteria when output quality is probabilistic, including a rubric section with pass thresholds in place of pixel-level specs.

items.title: Evals are the new unit tests: a working quality system for LLM features
items.snippet: A rigorous argument that teams shipping LLM features without a golden set are flying blind. Describes a three-tier stack (deterministic assertions, LLM-judge rubrics, a weekly 30-sample human audit) that caught 31 quality regressions in one quarter at a fintech before customers saw them.

items.title: Frontier price war: flagship model input pricing drops 60 percent overnight
items.snippet: The market leader cut input pricing from $1.10 to $0.45 per million tokens and output from $4.40 to $1.80, with two rivals signaling matching cuts within the week. Any AI feature proposal killed on unit economics last quarter deserves a rerun.

items.title: The interview snapshot: making weekly discovery compound instead of evaporate
items.snippet: An essay on why continuous discovery fails quietly: teams do the weekly calls but never synthesize. Proposes a one-page interview snapshot written within 24 hours of each call, and reports that in 9 of 11 teams studied the habit changed a real roadmap decision within six weeks.

items.title: Weekly roundup: 11 AI product launches you might have missed
items.snippet: A rapid-fire list covering launches from note-taking add-ons to yet another slide generator. Nothing category-defining, mostly incremental feature drops.

items.title: AI meeting notes come to every suite: a feature checklist comparison
items.snippet: A comparison table of meeting-notes features across four productivity suites. Concludes they are converging on the same checklist, with pricing the only real differentiator left.

items.title: How to run a quarterly roadmap review that stays strategic
items.snippet: Standard advice on pre-reads, timeboxing, and keeping status updates out of the room. Solid but familiar territory.

items.title: Conference recap: what stood out at this year's product summit
items.snippet: A recap of keynote themes: AI everywhere, platform consolidation, and the return of in-person workshops. Light on specifics.

items.title: The rise of the fractional CPO
items.snippet: Profiles of three fractional product leaders and how they structure engagements. Interesting industry context, limited immediate application.
